note: BAL-12 (2026-08-25). Every pill rule whose sizing DELIBERATELY differs from the voting-pill reference, with the reason. A pill is either RENDERING UNIFORM, OUT OF SCOPE WITH A REASON, or DIFFERING WITH NO REASON — and only the third is a defect. A reason is removed when its sizing difference or rule no longer exists.

reasons.reason: An ACTION pill, not a label. It carries a 44px tap target and reader-size type because a reader types into what it opens; the reference is a 22px non-tappable tag. The horizontal inset IS normalised to the action-pill inset (14px).
An ACTION pill with a 44px tap target. Its inset is normalised to 14px; its type is the section-title size deliberately, so the row reads as one of the sections around it (BC-21).
An ACTION pill with a 44px tap target — a phone number a reader taps. Inset normalised to 14px.

The PRIMARY door on the map. Making the primary control the size of a secondary one changes what the page means, not how it is spaced — and BAL-12 asks for uniform sizing where the difference has no reason, which this one does.

The zip chip INSIDE the ballot pill. It is sized against its parent rather than against the page, and matching it to the reference would make a nested control the same size as the thing containing it.
A superscript-scale note inside the ballot pill, not a pill in its own right despite the class name.
An ACTION pill in the ballot's top row, sized with its siblings in that row.
Zero padding on purpose: the wrapper hands its whole box to the trigger inside it, so padding here would double the inset.

LAY-12 replaces the expanded boundary card with an ACTION control on tablet and phone. It inherits the 44px minimum tap target and uses 13px text with 10px vertical/16px horizontal insets to stay compact beside Who Governs Here while naming the selected district. These component tokens derive from the spacing and detail/body scales; the smaller non-tappable vote tag is not its size reference.

Not the pill body: the Lumen horizon line at the base of the control (design handoff 2026-09-13), a 1px lit gradient. Its height is the hairline itself and is deliberately unrelated to the reference tag's height.
Not the pill body: the Lumen horizon line at the base of the ballot pill's zip half (design handoff 2026-09-13), a 1px lit gradient, sized as a hairline rather than against the reference tag.

An ACTION pill in the approved reader design (2026-09-28): Back, Details, Show on the map. It carries the 44px touch target and the design's 13px control type, because a reader taps it; the reference is a 22px non-tappable tag.

The map's selection pill (approved reader design, 2026-09-28) is a container holding a sentence and three action buttons, not a tag. Its inset and 14px type are the design's, so the sentence reads at body size above the map.

The Back to the map ACTION on the secondary pages (approved reader design, 2026-09-28): a 44px touch target with the design control type, because it is the way out of the page; the reference is a 22px non-tappable tag.
